questions.text: Six files F1, F2, F3, F4, F5 and F6 have 100, 200, 50, 80, 120, 150 records respectively. In what order should they be stored so as to optimize act. Assume each file is accessed with the same frequency
questions.solution:
With equal access frequency, the mean access time is smallest when shorter files come first (like shortest job first).

Order by size: F3 (50), F4 (80), F1 (100), F5 (120), F6 (150), F2 (200)

Answer: F3, F4, F1, F5, F6, F2

questions.text: How many 32K x 1 RAM chips are needed to provide a memory capacity of 256K-bytes?
questions.solution:
Required = 256K [latex]\times[/latex] 8 bits, one chip = 32K [latex]\times[/latex] 1 bit.

Chips = [latex]\frac{256K\times8}{32K\times1}=64[/latex]

Answer: 64

questions.text:
Consider the following code sequence having five instructions I1 to I5. Each of these instructions has the following format.

OP Ri, Rj, Rk

where operation OP is performed on contents of registers Rj and Rk and the result is stored in register Ri.

I1: ADD R1, R2, R3
I2: MUL R7, R1, R3
I3: SUB R4, R1, R5
I4: ADD R3, R2, R4
I5: MUL R7, R8, R9

Consider the following three statements.
S1: There is an anti-dependence between instructions l2 and l5
S2: There is an anti-dependence between instructions l2 and l4
S3: Within an instruction pipeline an anti-dependence always creates one or more stalls

Which one of above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Anti-dependence (WAR): a later instruction writes a register an earlier one reads.

- S1: I2 and I5 both write R7, which is output dependence, not anti [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False
- S2: I2 reads R3 and I4 writes R3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] anti-dependence [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- S3: in an in-order pipeline WAR causes no stall [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False

Answer: Only S2 is true

options: Only S1 and S3 are true
Only S2 and S3 are true

questions.text:
Consider the following reservation table for a pipeline having three stages S1,S2 and S3.

The minimum average latency (MAL) is ________.
questions.solution:
Forbidden latencies: S1 is used at 1 and 5 (gap 4); S2 at 2 and 4 (gap 2). Forbidden = {2, 4}, collision vector = 1010.

- Latency 3 again and again: CV stays 1011 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] cycle (3), average 3
- Cycle (1, 5): average 3

MAL = 3

Answer: 3

questions.text: Consider a machine with a byte addressable main memory of [latex]2^{20}[/latex]  bytes, block size of 16 bytes and a direct mapped cache having [latex]2^{12}[/latex] cache lines. Let the addresses of two consecutive bytes in main memory be [latex](E201F)_{16}[/latex] and [latex](E2020)_{16}[/latex]. What are the tag and cache line address (in hex) for main memory address [latex](E201F)_{16}[/latex]?
questions.solution:
Address = 20 bits: offset = 4 bits (16-byte block), line = 12 bits ([latex]2^{12}[/latex] lines), tag = 20 [latex]-[/latex] 16 = 4 bits.

E201F = E | 201 | F [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] tag = E, line = 201

Answer: E, 201
